results.summary: This Morse code trainer displays letters on a 7-segment display and requires the user to input the correct Morse pattern via a switch, providing immediate feedback. It progresses through the English alphabet as the user answers correctly. The design can be tested in simulation or on hardware, and it uses a 7-segment display and a switch as external components. It is an interactive educational game for learning Morse code.

This project is a gate test design that allows users to experiment with different logic gates by toggling switches and observing the outputs. It is built with Wokwi and includes interconnected gates between inputs and outputs. External hardware required includes switches and a single number LED display. It serves as an educational tool for understanding logic gate behavior.

This design generates a VGA video signal displaying a bouncing ROOTS logo with a kaleidoscope background. It is intended to be connected to a VGA monitor via the Tiny VGA Pmod. The design uses a 25.175 MHz clock and occupies a 2x2 tile area. It is a visual demo project for VGA output.

This design implements a variable-length LFSR with configurable 2-tap or 4-tap feedback, and includes hold and step controls. It produces a new LFSR value each clock cycle, with a valid signal indicating a properly configured LFSR. The design was tested using hand-generated top-level test modules with simulation tools. It is intended for use as a pseudo-random number generator or in testing applications.

Borg is a tiny GPU built around a RISC-V SoC (TinyQV) that renders a 10-frame animation of a rotating RGB triangle entirely in firmware. It uses a QSPI flash/PSRAM interface for program and data storage, and outputs UART for debug and communication. The design is implemented in Chisel and targets FPGA development with a pico-ice board and Raspberry Pi Debug Probe. It is notable for being a self-contained GPU demonstration on a small RISC-V platform.

This chip is a character-level language model that generates Shakespeare-like text using a ternary-weight transformer with all weights baked into ROM. It streams int16 residuals in and int8 residuals out, one token per transaction, and requires a host microcontroller to handle text encoding and decoding. The chip contains 22,400 ternary weights in 4,480 bytes of ROM and performs all arithmetic without multiplication. It is notable for being a complete neural network inference engine on a single chip with no weight loading.

This design implements a simplified 6502 processor with a subset of the original instruction set, built around an ALU, registers, and a microcoded instruction decoder. It is intended for educational purposes and includes detailed documentation on verification approaches. The processor operates at 40 MHz and uses a 1x2 tile area. It is notable for being a simplified version of the classic 6502 architecture.

This circuit generates Morse code for the letters J and R using a 4-bit synchronous counter and logic gates to simulate dots and dashes. It can be tested by connecting a 7-segment display and using a button to select between J and R. The design is a simple educational example of Morse code generation. External hardware includes a button, 7-segment display, and clock.

DUMBRV is a small RISC-V processor supporting the base RV32E instruction set plus Zicond and Zbs extensions, operating on two SPI memories. It uses one read-only SPI port for instructions and one read-write SPI port for data, both requiring 2-byte addresses. The processor is intended for use with SPI flash and RAM, and includes a test program in the repository. It is notable for being a minimal RISC-V implementation with external memory.

This design attempts to generate random numbers using the unstable state of a latch, with 34 instances per output pin to improve chances of randomness. When the freeze input is low, outputs toggle randomly; when high, outputs freeze. The design is experimental and may not work reliably due to potential bias. It is notable for its unconventional approach to random number generation.
